eyebrow: State and owner tag, per instance
code:
STATE=$(aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids "$ID" \
  --query "Reservations[0].Instances[0].State.Name" --output text)

OWNER=$(aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids "$ID" \
  --query "Reservations[0].Instances[0].Tags[?Key=='Owner'].Value | [0]" \
  --output text)

if [ "$OWNER" == "None" ]; then
  echo "MISSING TAG: $ID is $STATE with no Owner tag"
else
  echo "OK: $ID is $STATE, owned by $OWNER"
fi
caption: A missing AWS text value prints the literal word None — the check has to match that string, not -z.

code:
#!/bin/bash
INSTANCE_IDS=$(aws ec2 describe-instances \
  --query "Reservations[].Instances[].InstanceId" --output text)

for ID in $INSTANCE_IDS; do
  STATE=$(aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids "$ID" \
    --query "Reservations[0].Instances[0].State.Name" --output text)
  OWNER=$(aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids "$ID" \
    --query "Reservations[0].Instances[0].Tags[?Key=='Owner'].Value | [0]" \
    --output text)
  if [ "$OWNER" == "None" ]; then
    echo "MISSING TAG: $ID is $STATE with no Owner tag"
  else
    echo "OK: $ID is $STATE, owned by $OWNER"
  fi
done
caption: List, loop, check, report — the identical structure as Lesson 13's check-tags.sh, aimed at AWS.
